slides.title: Our starting hypothesis, "keep C", survived four of five tests; the fifth showed that keeping C unchanged is not enough

claims.claim: Initial hypothesis (set before testing): Vesper should retain C, because its low reported margin is an allocation effect rather than an avoidable economic cost.
Test 1: C earns more cash than its exit would save — Holds
evidence: C direct contribution $3.8M vs avoidable fixed cost $0.4M, so exit gives up a net $3.4M a year before any migration

claims.claim: Test 2: D cannot replace what C earns — Holds
evidence: Migration ceiling 25% of C revenue = $1.5M (all of D's spare capacity) x 50% = $0.75M, vs $3.4M at stake

claims.claim: Test 3: Exit costs and constraints bind — Holds
evidence: $2.1M first-year penalties vs $0.9M approved cash; C sits in 9 of 14 major bundles and no substitute is validated across every hospital model

claims.claim: Test 4: C is not driving customer attrition — Unproven
evidence: The 9-point renewal gap is correlational and confounded (size, legacy equipment, CS coverage); there is no before/after evidence either way

claims.claim: Test 5: Retaining C as-is is acceptable — Fails: refine
evidence: Bundle fill is 91% vs 95% required; C faces price pressure; a $1.25M a year redesign saving is available for $0.55M

claims.claim: Revised answer: Keep C, but not unchanged. Fund the C redesign, bring bundle fill back to 95%, use the renewals to open a consent-based path to D, and treat a 2029 sunset as a decision for Q4 2028, made on observed evidence. Test 4 stays open, and the plan includes a way to resolve it.

slides.title: C's 8% "gross margin" comes from the allocation: C earns $3.8M of direct contribution, and only $0.4M of its $3.3M allocated cost would go away if C exits

claims.claim: Two different margins.
evidence: Reported margin = (6.0 – 2.2 – 3.3) / 6.0 = 8.3%. Contribution margin = 3.8 / 6.0 = 63.3%.

Walk: Sales 6.0; Direct variable cost –2.2; Direct contribution 3.8 (63% of sales); Avoidable fixed cost –0.4; Profit lost if C exits 3.4; Shared cost that stays (reallocated) –2.9; Reported profit 0.5 (8.3% of sales)

claims.claim: 88% of the allocation stays.
evidence: $2.9M of the $3.3M is shared regulatory documentation and plant depreciation, spread by historical engineering hours. It does not go away when the SKU does.

claims.claim: Exit decisions turn on $3.4M.
evidence: Exiting C removes $3.8M of contribution and saves $0.4M of fixed cost, so Vesper loses $3.4M a year before any migration to D.
Decision-relevant figure: $3.4M a year of profit lost on exit, not 8%

claims.claim: The dashboard label misleads. The figure called "product gross margin" is measured after shared allocations, so it cannot be used to rank products for an exit or capacity decision.
evidence: Avoidable fixed cost of $0.40M per Finance; direct variable cost is fully avoidable if shipments end.

slides.title: On contribution, C is Vesper's strongest connector (63% vs D's 50%), and exiting it would move $2.9M of stranded cost onto A, B and D

claims.claim: On contribution, C is Vesper's strongest connector (63% vs D's 50%)
evidence: Margin by product, FY2026: Connector A (sales $14.0M) contribution 50%, reported 41%; Connector B (sales $9.0M) contribution 42%, reported 29%; Connector C (sales $6.0M) contribution 63%, reported 8.3%; Connector D (sales $4.0M) contribution 50%, reported 30%

claims.claim: the stranded cost does not go away when C does; it lands on A, B and D. B's reported margin would fall to about 17%, and the same margin-ranking logic would then pick B as the next "weakest" product. Total allocated cost falls by only $0.4M (from 6.5 to 6.1).
evidence: A: allocated 1.20 → 2.29; reported margin 41.4% → 33.7%
B: allocated 1.20 → 2.29; reported margin 28.9% → 16.8%
D (with 25% C migration): allocated 0.80 → 1.53; reported margin 30.0% → 22.3%
Total allocated: 3.20 → 6.10

claims.claim: Allocation basis: the pack says the remaining cost "would move to A, B and D" but does not give the split. We assume it moves pro rata to today's allocation (1.2 : 1.2 : 0.8).
evidence: D's figure includes $1.5M of migrated revenue at 50% contribution.

slides.title: Exiting C cuts cash contribution by $4.75M in its first year and $2.65M every year after, even if D wins the optimistic 25% of C revenue

claims.claim: Exiting C cuts cash contribution by $4.75M in its first year and $2.65M every year after
evidence: C direct contribution lost –3.80; Avoidable fixed cost saved +0.40; D migration at ceiling (25% x $6.0M x 50%) +0.75; Recurring annual impact –2.65; First-year bundle penalties (one-time) –2.10; First-year impact –4.75
Operating profit after allocations: Today (FY2026) 10.10; Exit C, 25% migration 7.45 (–26%); Exit C, no migration 6.70 (–34%)
Operating profit = total contribution 16.6 – allocated fixed 6.5. Exit case: contribution 16.6 – 3.8 + 0.75; fixed 6.5 – 0.4.

claims.claim: Penalties are one-time. Following Finance, the $2.1M is treated as a first-year cost, not recurring overhead. Even with every penalty waived, exit still loses $2.65M a year.
Migration is a ceiling, not a forecast.
evidence: The 25% comes from three sales interviews. It needs customer-specific adapters and validation.

claims.claim: Not yet costed: replacement qualification, clinical documentation, and any A/B accounts lost with the bundle.

slides.title: No migration rate makes exit pay: even if every C customer moved to D, Vesper would still lose $0.4M a year, and D can take only 25% today

claims.claim: Break-even requires the impossible
evidence: Impact = –3.8 + 0.4 + (share x $6.0M x 50%)
$6.8M of migrated D revenue needed to offset the $3.4M lost each year ($3.4M ÷ 50%). That is 113% of C's entire $6.0M revenue and 4.5x D's spare capacity.

claims.claim: Why D cannot close the gap: C's contribution margin (63%) is higher than D's incremental 50%, so each dollar moved from C to D earns less.
Migration crowds out D growth: the 25% ceiling would use all of D's $1.5M spare capacity, leaving no room for D's own organic growth.
The 25% is unobserved: it is the portfolio team's ceiling from three interviews. Finance has not estimated any recapture beyond it.
evidence: Bars beyond 25% (light, dashed) are hypothetical and exceed D's current capacity. Excludes the one-time $2.1M penalty.

slides.title: A 2027 exit would also break the board's non-negotiables: the penalty alone is 2.3x the approved cash, and C is in 9 of 14 major hospital bundles

claims.claim: ≥95% contracted bundle fill rate — Fails
evidence: 9 of 14 major hospital relationships specify a bundle containing C alongside A and B. No substitute for C has completed validation across every hospital model, so removing C leaves those bundles incomplete. Fill is already 91%.
Gap: Already –4 pts; would worsen

claims.claim: ≤$0.9M one-time cash for 2027 portfolio changes — Fails
evidence: First-year bundle penalties of $2.1M are payable unless counterparties consent. Replacement qualification and clinical documentation come on top and have not been costed.
Gap: ≥$1.2M over (2.3x)

claims.claim: Honour customer commitments — Fails
evidence: Exit requires notice, replacement qualification and clinical documentation. Two bundle agreements are being renewed now, so an exit notice would go into live negotiations.
Gap: Consent of 9 bundle customers needed

claims.claim: Judge on cash contribution, not the allocation report — Fails
evidence: Cash contribution falls by $3.4M a year before migration and $2.65M after the 25% ceiling, plus the $2.1M penalty in year one.
Gap: –$4.75M yr 1; –$2.65M a year after

claims.claim: Implication: a 2027 exit cannot go ahead without the board relaxing at least two of its own constraints. No other option on the table requires that (see page 12).
evidence: Assumes the $2.1M penalty counts against the 2027 one-time cash envelope because it is a direct cash consequence of the portfolio change.

slides.title: Moving the team to D cannot replace C: D's spare capacity caps the upside at $0.75M a year, and Vesper can capture that without exiting C

claims.claim: C's economics are 4.5x the most D can add without new capacity
evidence: C profit lost on exit (contribution – avoidable fixed): 3.40
Most D can add at present capacity ($1.5M revenue x 50%): 0.75

claims.claim: Known: D has room for $1.5M more revenue at present capacity. That room exists whether or not C exits. Under an exit, migrating C customers would fill it, crowding out D's own growth.
Known: the C redesign needs one design team for about four months (validation phase), then hands the team back.
Not known: the pack gives no quantified opportunity cost for those four months, and we do not invent one.

Illustrative ceiling only: suppose the team's absence delayed filling D's spare capacity by the full four months. The cost would then be at most 4/12 x $0.75M ≈ $0.25M, against $1.25M a year of redesign savings.
evidence: The $0.25M is a bound under a stated assumption, not an estimate of lost D sales.

claims.claim: Answer to "redeploy to D?": yes, but in sequence. The team works on the C redesign from March to June 2027 and moves to D (adapter validation and growth) from July.
D's "30% margin" is also after allocations. D's incremental contribution at existing capacity is 50%, still below C's 63%.
Growth is not replacement. D's double-digit market growth adds value at the margin. It does not justify giving up $3.8M of existing contribution (Finance's point).

slides.title: The 9-point renewal gap does not show C causes churn: C buyers are smaller, legacy-equipment, lower-coverage accounts, and nothing tests what removing C would do

claims.claim: Correlation, not causation. C accounts differ systematically in size, equipment age and service coverage. Each of these could lower renewal on its own.
evidence: Account buys C → Renews 9 pts less often (Claimed: C causes it)
Confounders named in the briefing pack: Smaller hospitals on legacy equipment; Lower customer-success coverage
Further plausible confounder: Bundle fill 91%, caused by A/B misses (our hypothesis, untested)
The 9 C-bundle customers are the ones receiving 91% fill, but the pack does not link this to renewals.

claims.claim: No counterfactual. The sample has no before/after evidence that removing C raises retention. It cannot support exit, and it cannot rule out a C effect either.
Tests to run before the Q4 2028 gate
evidence: Compare renewal within matched segments (size x equipment age x CS coverage)
Control for bundle fill each account actually received
Code lost-account exit reasons for any mention of C
Track retention of any accounts that drop C or move to D

claims.claim: Decision rule: only a renewal gap that persists within segments should feed the sunset decision, and then it should be valued against the $3.4M a year C contributes.

slides.title: The real service problem is bundle fill, at 91% against 95% contracted; A and B misses cause it and the C dashboard hides it, so exiting C would not fix it

claims.claim: The dashboard definition: C's 98% counts C as filled even when the bundle ships late because A or B is missing. The contract measures complete bundles, and that figure is 91%.
evidence: C on-time fill (service dashboard): 98%
Contracted bundle fill (actual): 91%
Contract minimum 95%; –4 pts

claims.claim: The cause sits in A and B, not C. Exiting C leaves the A/B misses in place and makes the nine C-bundles incomplete.
Fix the measure and the misses, not C
evidence: Redefine the KPI: make bundle-level contracted fill the headline service metric for every bundle customer. Report product-level fill only as a diagnostic.
Root-cause the A and B misses on the nine bundle accounts. Size buffer stock or allocation priority for A and B in those bundles.
Report monthly to the board until fill has stayed at 95% or above for two consecutive quarters.

claims.claim: Unknown: recovery speed. The pack does not say how fast bundle service can recover or what that costs. We have set a Q3 2027 target as a working assumption for Operations to confirm in February.

slides.title: Redesigning C is the only option that adds value and meets every constraint: +$2.4M over 2027–29, against –$8.7M for an immediate exit

claims.claim: Exit C in Q2 2027
evidence: Cash contribution vs retain unchanged: 2027 –3.43; 2028 –2.65; 2029 –2.65; cumulative 2027–29 –8.73 (–10.6 with no migration)
One-time cash vs $0.9M: ≥$2.1M penalties + qualification: fails
95% bundle fill: Worsens: no validated substitute
Customer commitments: Penalties unless 9 customers consent
Main risk: A/B bundle volume at risk (unquantified); B next 'weakest'

claims.claim: Retain C unchanged
evidence: Cash contribution: 0 / 0 / 0; cumulative 0
One-time cash: $0: meets
95% bundle fill: Needs A/B fix
Customer commitments: Honoured
Main risk: Price pressure erodes C; $1.25M saving forgone

claims.claim: Delayed sunset in 2029 (no redesign)
evidence: Cash contribution: 0 / 0 / 0; cumulative 0 (–2.65 to –3.4 a year from 2030)
One-time cash: $0 if exits match expiries: meets
95% bundle fill: Needs A/B fix; time to validate adapter
Customer commitments: Honoured; exit only at expiry
Main risk: As retain; locks in high-cost C until 2029

claims.claim: Redesign C now, 2029 sunset gate
evidence: Cash contribution: 2027 –0.13; 2028 +1.25; 2029 +1.25; cumulative +2.37 (downside +0.40)
One-time cash: $0.55M + $0.35M reserve: meets
95% bundle fill: Needs A/B fix (in plan)
Customer commitments: Honoured; renewals add D path
Main risk: Requalification delay at 2 customers; savings below estimate

claims.claim: Timing assumptions
evidence: exit effective 1 Jul 2027 (2027 loses half-year contribution, full $2.1M penalty); redesign savings from 1 Sep 2027 after validation and pilot. Migration at the 25% ceiling.

slides.title: The $0.55M redesign pays back in about 5 months of savings and still breaks even if it delivers only a fifth of the $1.25M estimate

claims.claim: Payback on run-rate savings ~5 months
evidence: $0.55M ÷ $1.25M a year = 0.44 years

claims.claim: 19% of estimated savings needed to break even by 2029
evidence: $0.55M ÷ 2.33 years of savings = $0.24M a year

claims.claim: +$0.40M 2027–29 value in the downside case
evidence: 50% of savings, 3 months late, full $0.9M envelope spent

claims.claim: Redesign scenarios: cash contribution vs retain unchanged, $M
evidence: Break-even: $0.24M a year from Sep 2027; $0.55M cost: –0.47; +0.24; +0.24; 0.00
Break-even with full $0.9M spent: $0.39M a year: –0.77; +0.39; +0.39; 0.00
Rounded. 2027 savings run Sep–Dec (4 months); window = 28 months = 2.33 years. Downside 2027: –0.90 + 0.63 x 1/12.

claims.claim: C's reported margin rises to ~29%, level with D's 30%, if the $1.25M comes out of direct cost. The ranking that started this debate goes away.
Operating profit rises 12%, from $10.1M to $11.35M a year at full run-rate.
Caution: $1.25M equals 57% of C's $2.2M direct cost, an engineering estimate at current volume. The two-site pilot exists to test it before the whole line converts.
evidence: Redesign cost excludes possible requalification tests at two customers; the downside case uses the $0.35M remaining in the envelope for them.

slides.title: Use the two renewals to secure C supply, bundle-level service terms and a consent-based path to D, not to give exit notice

claims.claim: 1. The two bundle renewals (Commercial + Legal; Q1 2027; terms set at Feb board)
evidence: Renew with C in the bundle; give no exit notice
Add a clause allowing substitution by a validated D + adapter only with customer consent, after qualification
Align term end with the 2029 expiry cohort so any sunset can happen at expiry, without penalty

claims.claim: 2. The other seven bundle customers (Account leads + Quality; Q1 2027)
evidence: Confirm C supply through current terms
Pre-notify the C design change and agree requalification tests early with the two customers that need them

claims.claim: 3. Bundle service recovery (Operations; Start Feb 2027; target ≥95% by Q3 2027)
evidence: Make bundle-level fill the contract KPI on every service dashboard
Root-cause A/B misses; set A/B buffer or allocation priority for bundle accounts; report monthly until ≥95%

claims.claim: 4. Penalty exposure (Finance; Ongoing)
evidence: Carry the $2.1M as a contingent one-time liability tied to premature termination, not as annual overhead (Finance's rule)

claims.claim: 5. D substitution evidence (Engineering (D) + Sales; From Jul 2027)
evidence: Run adapter and quality qualification with willing C customers; record actual acceptance, not interview estimates

claims.claim: Why this order: the penalty stands unless counterparties consent, so consent-based substitution and expiry-aligned terms are the only routes to a penalty-free exit later. Fixing A/B fill protects all nine bundles whatever happens to C.
evidence: Leads, and the Q3 2027 fill target, are proposals for management to confirm; the pack names neither owners nor a recovery date.

slides.title: A staged plan with two decision gates protects $3.8M of contribution today and keeps a 2029 sunset open if the evidence turns

claims.claim: Staged plan 2027–2029
evidence: C redesign: Design + validation; Pilot; Full line at run-rate savings (from Sep 2027)
Engineering team: On C; then On D: adapter validation and D growth
Bundle fill: A/B root-cause; recover to ≥95%; Sustain ≥95%; monthly board report
Contracts: Renew 2; Bundle terms run; requalification with 2 customers; 2029 expiries
D substitution evidence: Adapter qualification; observed acceptance rates; Only if Gate 2 passes: migrate at expiry
Assumes redesign kick-off in Mar 2027, 4-month validation, 2-month pilot.

claims.claim: Gate 1, end of Aug 2027: convert the whole C line?
evidence: Go if the pilot run-rate saving is ≥$0.4M a year (the break-even with the full $0.9M spent) and no customer requalification has failed
Otherwise stop at the pilot sites, with spend capped inside the $0.9M envelope

claims.claim: Gate 2, Q4 2028 (or the notice deadline, if earlier): sunset C in 2029?
evidence: Consider sunset only if: D adapter validated on every hospital model in C bundles; observed acceptance high enough; D capacity in place; fill ≥95% for 2 quarters; renewal gap shown to be causal; updated exit bridge positive
Contract notice periods are not in the pack; Gate 2 must precede them.

slides.title: None of the open unknowns is likely to flip the decision against exit, and each is tested at a gate in the plan

claims.claim: D substitution acceptance — Effect: None: even 100% migration loses $0.4M a year
evidence: 25% is a ceiling from three sales interviews; adapters and validation are customer-specific
Resolved by: Observed acceptance in qualification (from Jul 2027)

claims.claim: Requalification at 2 customers — Effect: Low: downside (3 months late, $0.9M spent, half the savings) is still +$0.40M
evidence: Not included in the $0.55M; could delay savings
Resolved by: Early engagement in Q1 2027; $0.35M reserve

claims.claim: Redesign savings at scale — Effect: Low: breaks even at 19% of estimate (31% if the full $0.9M is spent)
evidence: $1.25M is an estimate at current volume, 57% of C's direct cost
Resolved by: Two-site pilot; Gate 1 threshold $0.4M a year

claims.claim: Speed of bundle-fill recovery — Effect: Same under every option, since the cause is A/B; matters for renewals
evidence: Fill is 91% vs 95%; no recovery timeline or cost in the pack
Resolved by: Ops plan in Feb; monthly board tracking

claims.claim: Engineering opportunity cost — Effect: Low: illustrative ceiling ≈$0.25M vs $1.25M a year of savings
evidence: Not quantified for the four months on C
Resolved by: Team moves to D from Jul 2027

claims.claim: C price pressure — Effect: Exit breaks even on run-rate only if C contribution falls ~70%, from $3.8M to $1.15M
evidence: Competitive pressure named, not quantified
Resolved by: Re-test C contribution at Gate 2
C price-pressure threshold: exit run-rate = –C contribution + 0.4 + 0.75 = 0, so C contribution = $1.15M.

claims.claim: Key assumptions: FY2026 volumes and costs hold through 2029; the penalty is payable in full unless counterparties consent; the $0.4M avoidable fixed cost is Finance's estimate; cash effects are undiscounted (the horizon is three years).

slides.title: We ask the board for six decisions that keep $3.8M of contribution, avoid $2.1M of penalties and add about $1.25M a year

claims.claim: Reject discontinuing connector C in 2027
evidence: Exit loses $4.75M in year one and $2.65M a year after, and breaches the cash and fill constraints

claims.claim: Approve $0.55M for the C redesign, plus up to $0.35M reserve, within the $0.9M envelope
evidence: Pilot at two sites first; Gate 1 at end of Aug 2027

claims.claim: Mandate bundle-level contracted fill as the service KPI
evidence: Operations to present an A/B recovery plan to reach ≥95%, with dates and cost

claims.claim: Authorise renewal terms for the two bundle agreements
evidence: C retained; consent-based D substitution clause; terms aligned to 2029 expiries

claims.claim: Sequence engineering: C redesign Mar–Jun 2027, then D
evidence: The D adapter work also builds the evidence for any later sunset

claims.claim: Set Gate 2 criteria for any 2029 sunset (Q4 2028)
evidence: Validated adapter, observed acceptance, sustained ≥95% fill, causal renewal test, positive exit bridge

slides.title: Every number in the deck comes from briefing-pack inputs with the arithmetic shown here

claims.claim: Margins (FY2026, $M)
evidence: Contribution margin = (sales – direct variable) / sales: A 7.0/14.0 = 50.0%; B 3.8/9.0 = 42.2%; C 3.8/6.0 = 63.3%; D 2.0/4.0 = 50.0%
Reported margin = (sales – variable – allocated) / sales: A 5.8/14.0 = 41.4%; B 2.6/9.0 = 28.9%; C 0.5/6.0 = 8.3%; D 1.2/4.0 = 30.0%
C allocated 3.3 = avoidable 0.4 + non-avoidable 2.9 (88%)
Company: contribution 16.6 – allocated 6.5 = operating profit 10.1

claims.claim: Exit bridge
evidence: First 12 months: –2.65 – 2.1 penalty = –4.75
Break-even migrated D revenue = 3.4 / 0.5 = 6.8 = 113% of C sales, 4.5x D spare capacity of 1.5
Operating profit after exit: 16.6 – 3.8 + 0.75 = 13.55 contribution – 6.1 fixed = 7.45 (–26%); no migration 6.7 (–34%)

claims.claim: Reallocation if C exits (pro rata assumption)
Redesign
evidence: Payback = 0.55 / 1.25 = 0.44 yr ≈ 5.3 months of run-rate
Reported C margin after redesign = (6.0 – 0.95 – 3.3)/6.0 = 29.2%; operating profit 10.1 + 1.25 = 11.35 (+12%)

claims.claim: Other bounds
evidence: Engineering ceiling = 4/12 x 0.75 = 0.25; C price-pressure break-even: 3.8 – 1.15 = 2.65 drop (70%)

slides.title: Where the pack was silent we made eight working assumptions; each is conservative or does not change the answer

claims.claim: Exit timing: Exit effective 1 Jul 2027 ("Q2 2027"); the full $2.1M penalty falls in 2027
evidence: Exit looks no better under any timing; recurring loss is timing-independent

claims.claim: Penalty and cash envelope: The $2.1M penalty counts against the $0.9M one-time cash for 2027 portfolio changes
evidence: Even outside the envelope, exit fails the fill and contribution tests

claims.claim: Migration: 25% migration used as a ceiling, never a forecast; no recapture beyond it
evidence: 100% migration still loses $0.4M a year

claims.claim: Reallocation split: The $2.9M of stranded cost moves pro rata to today's A/B/D allocation
evidence: Illustrative only; total company profit is unaffected by the split

claims.claim: Redesign timing: Kick-off Mar 2027, 4-month validation, 2-month two-site pilot, savings from Sep 2027
evidence: Pilot-site savings in Jul–Aug ignored (conservative)

claims.claim: Savings location: The $1.25M direct saving reduces C's direct cost (used only for the 29% reported-margin figure)
evidence: Cash case is unchanged wherever the saving sits

claims.claim: Delayed sunset: Exits at contract expiry in 2029 avoid the penalty; contracts not expiring would still need consent
evidence: Only affects the post-2029 view

claims.claim: Horizon and discounting: 2027–29, undiscounted; FY2026 volumes, prices and costs held flat
evidence: A short horizon and early redesign cash flows mean discounting would not change the ranking

claims.claim: No questions could be put to management while preparing this deck; these choices should be confirmed with Finance and Operations.

normalized.recommendation: Do not discontinue C in 2027. Redesign C now (+$2.4M over 2027–29), recover bundle fill, then hand the team to D; renew the two bundles without exit notice and with a consent-based D path; hold a Q4 2028 gate on a 2029 sunset. Board decisions requested: (1) Reject discontinuing connector C in 2027; (2) Approve $0.55M for the C redesign, plus up to $0.35M reserve, within the $0.9M envelope; (3) Mandate bundle-level contracted fill as the service KPI; (4) Authorise renewal terms for the two bundle agreements; (5) Sequence engineering: C redesign Mar–Jun 2027, then D; (6) Set Gate 2 criteria for any 2029 sunset (Q4 2028).

alternatives_considered.option: Exit C in Q2 2027 (discontinue C and redeploy the team to D)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: –$8.73M cumulative 2027–29 (–10.6 with no migration); loses $4.75M in year one and $2.65M a year after; ≥$2.1M penalties + qualification fails the $0.9M cash constraint; bundle fill worsens with no validated substitute; penalties unless 9 customers consent. 'A 2027 exit cannot go ahead without the board relaxing at least two of its own constraints.'

Not chosen: 0 cash impact vs baseline and meets cash/commitment constraints, but needs A/B fix; main risk 'Price pressure erodes C; $1.25M saving forgone'. Hypothesis test 5 'Retaining C as-is is acceptable' — 'Fails: refine'.
Not chosen: 0 cash impact 2027–29 (–2.65 to –3.4 a year from 2030); $0 one-time cash if exits match expiries; main risk 'As retain; locks in high-cost C until 2029'.

Chosen: 'the only option that adds value and meets every constraint: +$2.4M over 2027–29' (+2.37, downside +0.40); $0.55M + $0.35M reserve meets the envelope; main risk 'Requalification delay at 2 customers; savings below estimate'.

alternatives_considered.option: Redeploy the engineering team to D
alternatives_considered.treatment: 'yes, but in sequence. The team works on the C redesign from March to June 2027 and moves to D (adapter validation and growth) from July.' D's spare capacity caps the upside at $0.75M a year, capturable without exiting C.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: The 25% migration is a ceiling from three sales interviews, not a forecast; it needs customer-specific adapters and validation; Finance has not estimated any recapture beyond it.
Not yet costed: replacement qualification, clinical documentation, and any A/B accounts lost with the bundle.
The $2.1M penalty counts against the 2027 one-time cash envelope because it is a direct cash consequence of the portfolio change; penalty is payable in full unless counterparties consent.
The $2.9M stranded cost is assumed to move pro rata to today's allocation (1.2 : 1.2 : 0.8); the pack does not give the split.
The pack gives no quantified opportunity cost for the four months the team spends on C; illustrative ceiling ≈$0.25M.
The 9-point renewal gap is correlational and confounded (size, legacy equipment, CS coverage); there is no before/after evidence either way. Bundle fill as a confounder is 'our hypothesis, untested'.
Unknown: recovery speed of bundle fill; Q3 2027 target is a working assumption for Operations to confirm in February.
$1.25M redesign saving equals 57% of C's $2.2M direct cost, an engineering estimate at current volume; redesign cost excludes possible requalification tests at two customers.
C price pressure is named but not quantified; exit breaks even on run-rate only if C contribution falls ~70%, from $3.8M to $1.15M.
Exit effective 1 Jul 2027; redesign kick-off Mar 2027, 4-month validation, 2-month pilot, savings from 1 Sep 2027.
Contract notice periods are not in the pack; Gate 2 must precede them.
Exits at contract expiry in 2029 avoid the penalty; contracts not expiring would still need consent.
FY2026 volumes, prices and costs held flat through 2029; the $0.4M avoidable fixed cost is Finance's estimate; cash effects are undiscounted (2027–29 horizon).
Leads and the Q3 2027 fill target are proposals for management to confirm; the pack names neither owners nor a recovery date.
No questions could be put to management while preparing this deck; these choices should be confirmed with Finance and Operations.
